args: Inspect the overflow-checking design for bit readers in src/bits.c, especially CHK_OVERFLOW and bit_read_B. What exact root-cause fix safely rejects an empty cursor at byte == size while preserving valid reads near EOF? Are there callers or semantics (error flags/cursor behavior) that make changing the common macro risky?

The supplied ASan report shows a one-byte heap-buffer-overflow in src/bits.c:bit_read_B when the Bit_Chain cursor is exactly dat->byte == dat->size and dat->bit == 0. The vulnerability description says CHK_OVERFLOW uses strict greater-than comparisons and therefore accepts that EOF cursor, after which bit_read_B dereferences dat->chain[dat->byte]. The path is malformed R13/R2000 header-variable decoding via decode_R13_R2000 and FIELD_B for DIMSOXD. I have not edited anything yet. I want to determine whether the common macro should be corrected globally or whether bit_read_B needs a targeted guard, and understand expected overflow signaling and boundary semantics for multi-bit readers.
